title: Organisational Leadership
summary: Leadership = interpersonal process of influence that motivates others toward goals reflecting leader/organisational values（人际过程、影响、激励、目标与价值四要素）
Formal authority ≠ leadership influence：职位授予分配任务和资源的权利；实际领导影响可来自没有头衔的人，管理与领导可以重叠
Leader emergence（谁被认可/选为领导）≠ leader effectiveness（实际成果、成员发展、公平与长期后果）；自信、可见度帮助涌现但不保证有效
Born or made：特质较稳定，行为与技能可学习；Judge et al. (2002) Big Five 元分析——外向性正向关联最强，尽责性、开放性正向，宜人性较弱，神经质负向
Trait approach 的局限：不直接解释行为、对涌现和有效性关系不同、不诊断情境、易被误读为领导无法培养；相关 ≠ 因果
Behavioural approach：consideration（关系行为）与 initiating structure（任务行为）是两个独立维度，可同时高或同时低；Judge, Piccolo & Ilies (2004)：关怀↔满意度/动机/感知有效性，任务结构↔领导工作绩效与团队/组织绩效稍强
Hersey–Blanchard：readiness = 针对具体任务的 ability（知识+技能）+ willingness（动机+信心）；R1→S1 Telling（高指导/较低支持）、R2→S2 Selling（高指导/高支持）、R3→S3 Participating（较低指导/高支持）、R4→S4 Delegating（较低指导/较低支持）
R2 = 不会做但愿意；R3 = 会做但不愿/不自信——最易混淆；Delegating ≠ 撒手不管，须约定成果、期限、决策权限与汇报节点
Thompson & Vecchio (2009)：情境领导模型只得到有限支持，修订版预测不如原版；处方是待验证的假设，不是唯一规定
Fiedler：LPC 量表评价最不愿共事的同事；低 LPC = 任务导向，高 LPC = 关系导向；LPC 是相对稳定的动机取向，不是当前团队关系指标
Situational favourability = leader–member relations + task structure + position power → 八情境 I–VIII；I–II 很有利、VII–VIII 很不利时任务导向较好，III–VI 中间时关系导向较好；I 职位权力强、II 弱
Fiedler 的干预思路是改变情境（澄清授权、修复关系）或调整领导任用，而不是要求领导临时改变取向；授权不能替代信任修复
五种当代方式：Level 5（Collins 2001，个人谦逊+专业意志）、Servant（支持成长但保留标准与问责）、Authentic（自我意识、平衡处理、关系透明、内化道德视角）、Transformational（四个 I）、Transactional（条件性奖励、主动/被动例外管理）
Power = 不对称控制他人重视的资源与后果；Status = 他人给予的尊重与敬佩；两者可以分离；Galinsky et al. (2006)：权力条件下换位思考减少（额头写 E 任务）

concepts.def: An interpersonal process of influence that motivates others to put in effort to achieve goals reflecting the values of the leader or organisation.
concepts.defZh: 通过人际影响激励他人努力实现体现领导者或组织价值的目标；四要素：interpersonal process、influence、motivation、goals and values。
concepts.one: 领导力就是通过影响和激励别人，一起去实现体现领导者或组织价值的目标。
concepts.eg: 团队做客户报告时，负责人先讲清报告用来干什么，再商量分工，还帮有困难的同事。
concepts.like: 像领队先说清目的地和路线，再带着大家一起走到终点。

concepts.def: Whether a person is recognised or selected as a leader.
concepts.defZh: 谁被认可或选为领导；自信、可见度、外向性有助于涌现，但不保证有效。
concepts.one: 领导涌现指的是谁被大家认可或选成了领导，被选上不等于带得好。
concepts.eg: 小组讨论时最先自信发言的同学，很快就被大家推成了组长，至于带得好不好还不知道。
concepts.like: 像先站上舞台的人先拿到聚光灯，演得好不好是另一回事。

concepts.def: How well a leader actually leads the team and what outcomes result.
concepts.defZh: 看任务成果、成员发展、公平待遇和长期后果（信任、合作、伦理）。
concepts.one: 领导有效性看的是实际带出了什么：任务成果、成员成长、公平和长期信任。
concepts.eg: 组长不只是按时交了报告，还分工公平、肯听反对意见，组员也真的学到了东西。
concepts.like: 像评价教练要看整季战绩和球员进步，而不是看他嗓门大不大。

concepts.def: Studies links between relatively stable personal characteristics and leader emergence or effectiveness.
concepts.defZh: Judge 等（2002）Big Five 元分析：外向性最强正向，尽责性、开放性正向，宜人性较弱，神经质负向；只是平均倾向，不是个人保证。
concepts.one: 特质取向研究稳定的人格特点和当领导的关系，只说平均倾向，不保证某个人。
concepts.eg: Judge 等（2002）发现外向性和领导的关联最强，但外向的人不一定就能把团队带好。
concepts.like: 像鲜艳的队服让球员更显眼，但球踢得好不好还要看场上。

concepts.def: Showing concern and respect for followers by listening, valuing their views and recognising contributions.
concepts.defZh: 倾听、尊重、认可贡献和一致行动建立信任；与满意度、动机、感知有效性关联更强。倾听不等于取消标准。
concepts.one: 关怀行为是关心和尊重下属：倾听意见、认可贡献、说到做到，以此建立信任。
concepts.eg: 成员多次迟交，领导先问他遇到了什么困难、需要什么支持，同时也讲清下一步要负的责任。
concepts.like: 像教练先了解队员伤情再安排训练，但比赛要求并不降低。

concepts.def: Clarifying roles, priorities, standards and how progress will be checked.
concepts.defZh: 明确职责、优先级、标准和检查方式；与领导工作绩效、团队/组织绩效关联稍强。与关怀是两个独立维度。
concepts.one: 任务结构行为是把职责、优先级、标准和检查方式讲清楚，让大家知道怎么干。
concepts.eg: 展示小组先定好研究问题、每人分工和整合的时间表，再按节点检查进度。
concepts.like: 像乐队先排好每人的乐段、节拍和合练时间，才能合奏成曲。

concepts.def: A follower's ability (knowledge and skill) and willingness (motivation and confidence) to perform a specific task.
concepts.defZh: 针对具体任务，不是年龄、职称或资历的永久标签；同一人在不同任务上准备度可能不同。
concepts.one: 准备度是员工做某项具体任务的能力和意愿，换一项任务就要重新判断。
concepts.eg: 员工做常规财务报告很熟练，换到一个陌生的演示平台就既不会做也没把握。
concepts.like: 像开了多年车的老司机，第一次开船照样是新手。

concepts.def: High task direction, lower relationship support; matched to R1 (low ability, low willingness).
concepts.defZh: 给出清楚具体指令、示范第一步、频繁检查；较低支持仍要尊重员工。
concepts.one: 指示型针对不会做又没信心的人（R1）：给具体指令和示范，经常检查。
concepts.eg: 新员工没用过报告系统，主管先示范第一步，给出明确的指令，再确认他真的听懂了。
concepts.like: 像教小孩骑车：先扶着车把一步步示范，而不是说「自己骑吧」。

concepts.def: High task direction and high relationship support; matched to R2 (low ability, high willingness).
concepts.defZh: 解释做法与理由、鼓励学习、认可进展；selling 指 explaining，不是施压或对外销售。
concepts.one: 解释型针对不会做但很想学的人（R2）：详细指导加鼓励，还解释为什么。
concepts.eg: 热情的实习生想写好第一份客户报告，主管给范例、讲清每部分的目的，还夸他有进步。
concepts.like: 像带热情的新学徒：边讲原理边手把手教，还常夸他进步了。

concepts.def: Lower task direction, high relationship support; matched to R3 (high ability, low willingness/confidence).
concepts.defZh: 讨论顾虑、探索选项、让员工参与计划；不必重教基础步骤。
concepts.one: 参与型针对会做但没信心的人（R3）：少讲步骤，多听顾虑，请他一起规划。
concepts.eg: 资深员工会写报告，但一次难缠的客户会后不愿牵头了，主管和他聊顾虑、问需要什么支持。
concepts.like: 像对待状态低迷的老将：不用重教动作，而是陪他找回信心。

concepts.def: Lower task direction and lower relationship support; matched to R4 (high ability, high willingness).
concepts.defZh: 约定成果、期限、决策权限，让员工选方法；领导仍可联系，问责清楚，不是撒手不管。
concepts.one: 授权型针对又会做又愿做的人（R4）：约定成果、期限和权限，方法由他定。
concepts.eg: 分析师多次成功完成类似任务，主管只约定交付物和截止日期，方法让他自定，按节点汇报。
concepts.like: 像把车钥匙交给老司机：说好目的地和到达时间，路线他自己定。

concepts.def: Fiedler's measure in which a leader describes the coworker they worked least well with, identifying a relatively stable motivational orientation.
concepts.defZh: 评价较负面 → 低 LPC → 任务导向；评价较正面 → 高 LPC → 关系导向；不是当前团队关系指标。
concepts.one: LPC 量表让领导评价最难合作的同事，由此判断他偏任务型还是关系型。
concepts.eg: 一位领导对合作最不顺的同事仍评价得比较正面，这就是高 LPC，属于关系导向。
concepts.like: 像看人怎么评价最难合作的队友：还能说出优点的更看重关系。

concepts.def: The degree of control a leader has, determined by leader–member relations, task structure and position power.
concepts.defZh: 三因素组合为八情境 I–VIII；两端（很有利/很不利）任务导向较好，中间关系导向较好。
concepts.one: 情境有利程度指领导能掌控多少局面，看上下级关系、任务结构和职位权力。
concepts.eg: 团队信任主管、任务也清楚，但调资源要逐项审批：关系和结构有利，职位权力却弱。
concepts.like: 像开车顺不顺：乘客配不配合、路线清不清楚、方向盘在不在手里。

concepts.def: Formal authority over rewards, punishments, task assignment and related decisions.
concepts.defZh: Fiedler 三因素之一；关系好不等于权力强，加强授权也不会自动产生信任。
concepts.one: 职位权力是职位本身带来的正式权力，比如能奖惩、派任务和调资源。
concepts.eg: 项目协调员想调人手和预算，却要先经几个部门负责人批准，说明他的职位权力弱。
concepts.like: 像手里有没有钥匙：有钥匙能开门，但不代表大家愿意跟你进门。

concepts.def: Collins' (2001) description of leaders who combine personal humility with professional will.
concepts.defZh: 承认错误、分享功劳，又坚定推动长期成果；发展接班人与系统。五层图不是普遍职级排名。
concepts.one: 第五级领导是个人谦逊加上专业意志：肯认错、让功劳，又坚定推动长期成果。
concepts.eg: 新流程失败后，领导承认自己的假设不完整，把功劳归给找出问题的员工，再定目标持续跟进。
concepts.like: 像肯认错改路线、却一定要把队伍带到终点的领队。

concepts.def: Prioritising followers' growth, capability and wellbeing while considering responsibilities to the organisation and wider community.
concepts.defZh: 倾听、辅导、分享信息、移除障碍；仍保留标准与问责，不等于批准每项请求。
concepts.one: 服务型领导把下属的成长和福祉放在优先位置，但工作标准和问责照样保留。
concepts.eg: 好几个人想在同一班次休假，主管先听理由，说明服务不能停，再一起商量换班。
concepts.like: 像为别人搭台阶帮他往上走，但台阶通向的方向不变。

concepts.def: Leadership based on self-awareness, balanced processing, relational transparency and an internalised moral perspective.
concepts.defZh: 行动与反思过的价值一致；真实不能为羞辱开脱，要看持续可观察的行为。
concepts.one: 真实型领导看清自己、全面看证据、适度坦诚，行动和反思过的价值观一致。
concepts.eg: 经理公开说自己方案的不足，请大家提反对证据，再按事先讲明的原则做决定。
concepts.like: 像先照镜子看清自己，再按心里的指南针校准方向。

concepts.def: Inspiring and developing followers toward a shared vision through idealised influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation and individualised consideration.
concepts.defZh: 四个 I：榜样、鼓舞性动机、智力激发、个别化关怀；喊口号或自信本身不够。
concepts.one: 变革型领导用共同愿景激励人，靠榜样、鼓舞、启发思考和个别关怀发展成员。
concepts.eg: 改进服务时，主管讲清改变能帮到哪些顾客，鼓励员工质疑现有障碍，还按各人需要辅导。
concepts.like: 像既指明远方目的地、又教每个人学会走路的向导。

concepts.def: Clarifying performance expectations, linking achievement to rewards (contingent reward) and managing deviations (active/passive management by exception).
concepts.defZh: 主动例外管理：持续监测并及时纠正；被动例外管理：问题出现后才介入。与变革型可互补，不是互斥的人。
concepts.one: 交易型领导事先讲清绩效期望和回报，达标就兑现，出了偏差就介入纠正。
concepts.eg: 经理事先和团队约定交付目标和认可方式，团队达标后就按约定兑现奖励。
concepts.like: 像赛前讲清计分规则和奖金，按成绩发奖，有人犯规再吹哨。

concepts.def: Power is asymmetric control over valued resources and outcomes; status is the respect and admiration others grant.
concepts.defZh: 两者可分离：有职权仍可能缺少信任，受尊重也可能没有审批权；权力可能降低换位思考（Galinsky 等 2006）。
concepts.one: 权力是能控制别人在乎的资源和后果，地位是别人给你的尊重，两者可以分开。
concepts.eg: 新经理能批预算、派项目，这是权力；大家有难题都去请教资深同事，这是他的地位。
concepts.like: 像一个人握着开门的钥匙，另一个人是大家信任的向导。

tf.q: A person without a formal managerial title cannot provide leadership in a team.
tf.exp: 没有头衔也能领导。职位只给你分配任务和资源的权利，真正的领导影响可以来自经验和信任。

tf.q: Leader emergence and leader effectiveness are different: being chosen as leader does not guarantee leading the team well.
tf.exp: 被选为领导只说明你「涌现」了；带得好不好要看成果、成员成长、公平和长期后果。

tf.q: According to the Big Five meta-analysis by Judge et al. (2002) presented in class, agreeableness showed the strongest positive relationship with leadership.
tf.exp: 关联最强的是外向性（extraversion），宜人性关联较弱，神经质则是负向关联。

tf.q: Consideration and initiating structure are two ends of a single continuum, so increasing one necessarily reduces the other.
tf.exp: 关怀和任务结构是两个独立维度，可以同时高或同时低；把任务讲清楚并不会减少关心。

tf.q: Judge, Piccolo and Ilies (2004) found that consideration was more strongly related to follower satisfaction and motivation than initiating structure was.
tf.exp: 关怀与满意度、动机和感知有效性联系更强；任务结构则与领导和团队的绩效联系稍强。

tf.q: In the Hersey–Blanchard model, an employee's readiness is task-specific, so the same person can be R4 on one task and R1 or R2 on another.
tf.exp: 准备度看的是做某项具体任务的能力和意愿，不是贴在人身上的永久标签。

tf.q: An R3 follower is unable to do the task but is enthusiastic and confident.
tf.exp: 不会做但热情自信的是 R2；R3 正好相反，是会做但不太愿意或没信心。

tf.q: The Delegating (S4) style means the leader no longer needs to be available or hold the follower accountable.
tf.exp: 授权不是撒手不管：仍要约定成果、期限、决策权限和汇报节点，领导也要能被找到。

tf.q: Thompson and Vecchio (2009) found only limited support for situational leadership theory, and the revised version predicted outcomes less well than the original.
tf.exp: 研究只找到有限支持，修订版的预测还不如原版，所以模型的处方只能算待验证的假设。

tf.q: In Fiedler's model, a high LPC score indicates that the leader currently has poor relationships with team members.
tf.exp: 高 LPC 只说明这位领导偏关系导向，这是一种稳定取向，不反映他现在和团队关系好坏。

tf.q: Fiedler's situations I and II both have good leader–member relations and a structured task, but position power is strong in I and weak in II.
tf.exp: 两种情境都是关系好、任务结构化，区别只在职位权力：情境 I 强，情境 II 弱。

tf.q: According to Fiedler's pattern, relationship-oriented leaders perform better in very favourable situations (I–II).
tf.exp: 关系导向在中间情境（III–VI）更好；两端很有利或很不利时，任务导向更好。

tf.q: Strengthening a leader's formal position power will automatically repair poor leader–member relations.
tf.exp: 权力变大不会自动带来信任。修复关系要靠兑现承诺，并公平地让成员参与决策。

tf.q: Active management by exception involves monitoring for deviations and correcting them, whereas passive management by exception waits until problems occur.
tf.exp: 两者差在介入时机：主动型持续监测、发现偏差就纠正，被动型要等问题出现了才处理。

tf.q: Social status refers to the respect and admiration others give a person, and a person can have high status without control over budgets.
tf.exp: 地位来自别人给你的尊重，权力来自对资源和后果的控制，两者可以分开，没预算也能有地位。

mcq.q: A new graduate has never used the company's reporting system, is unsure where to start and seems hesitant to try. According to Hersey and Blanchard, which style is recommended?
options: Selling (S2)
Telling (S1)
Participating (S3)
Delegating (S4)
mcq.exp: 这名新人既不会用系统又没信心，属于 R1，要用指示型：给具体指令、示范第一步、经常检查。

mcq.q: An enthusiastic intern is eager to write her first client report but does not understand report structure or how to evaluate evidence. Which readiness level and style best fit?
options: R3 – Participating
R1 – Telling
R4 – Delegating
R2 – Selling
mcq.exp: 实习生不会做但很想学，是 R2，要用解释型：详细指导加鼓励，讲清理由、讨论草稿。热情替代不了技能。

mcq.q: An experienced analyst knows exactly how to write the report but has become reluctant to lead after a difficult client meeting. What should the leader mainly do?
options: Discuss her concerns, explore options together and involve her in planning, with less detailed direction
Re-teach the basic steps of report writing with frequent checks
Hand over the task with no further contact
Explain the reasons for each step and give high direction
mcq.exp: 分析师会做但失去了信心，是 R3，要用参与型：少指导、多支持，听她的顾虑。重教基础步骤解决不了真正的问题。

mcq.q: Which statement about the Delegating (S4) style is most accurate?
options: The leader withdraws completely and lets the follower act without limits
The leader provides high support but low direction
The leader agrees outcomes, deadlines and decision limits, then lets the follower choose the method
The leader explains each step and checks frequently
mcq.exp: 授权型是指导和支持都较少，但仍要先约定成果、期限和决策权限，并说好汇报方式；完全撤出不是授权。

mcq.q: On Fiedler's LPC scale, a leader describes their least preferred coworker in relatively favourable terms. What does the model infer?
options: Low LPC – task-motivated orientation
High LPC – relationship-motivated orientation
The leader currently has good leader–member relations
The leader should use the Selling style
mcq.exp: 对最不愿共事的同事评价还比较正面，就是高 LPC，属于关系导向。它测的是稳定取向，不是现在的团队关系。

mcq.q: A team has good leader–member relations, an unstructured task and strong position power. Which Fiedler situation is this?
options: Situation II
Situation V
Situation IV
Situation III
mcq.exp: 关系好、任务不结构化、权力强，就是情境 III。情境 IV 只差在权力弱，情境 II 是任务结构化但权力弱。

mcq.q: According to the Fiedler pattern presented in class, which leader is predicted to perform relatively better in situation V (poor relations, structured task, strong power)?
options: A relationship-oriented (high LPC) leader
A task-oriented (low LPC) leader
Any leader, because situation V is very favourable
A leader using the Delegating style
mcq.exp: 情境 V 属于中间有利程度（III–VI），这一段关系导向表现更好；任务导向是在两端很有利或很不利时更好。

mcq.q: A project coordinator knows what to deliver but cannot obtain resources or resolve departmental priority conflicts, and the team distrusts him. Consistent with Fiedler's logic, what is the most appropriate intervention?
options: Require him to switch immediately to a relationship orientation
Give him more authority, which will automatically restore trust
Clarify his decision authority and separately rebuild relations by following through on commitments and involving members fairly
Diagnose his followers as R1 and use Telling
mcq.exp: Fiedler 的思路是改变情境来改善匹配：授权解决权力问题，修复关系要另外做，不能指望领导临时改变稳定取向。

mcq.q: What is the key difference between the Hersey–Blanchard model and Fiedler's contingency model?
options: Hersey–Blanchard focuses on position power; Fiedler on follower willingness
Hersey–Blanchard has the leader adjust direction and support to follower readiness; Fiedler matches a relatively stable orientation to the situation
Both assume the leader's style is fixed and cannot change
Fiedler measures readiness with the LPC scale
mcq.exp: 前者让领导按下属准备度调整指导和支持；Fiedler 认为取向较稳定，要靠改变情境或调整任用来匹配。

mcq.q: After a new service process fails, a CEO publicly admits her assumptions were incomplete, credits staff for identifying the problems, then sets firm improvement targets and follows up relentlessly. This best illustrates:
options: Passive management by exception
Servant leadership
Level 5 leadership
Contingent reward
mcq.exp: 这就是第五级领导：个人谦逊（承认错误、把功劳给员工）加专业意志（定目标并坚持推动）。服务型领导重点是支持下属成长。

mcq.q: Several staff request leave on the same shift. A servant leader would most likely:
options: Approve every request to show care
Refuse all requests to protect operations
Delegate the decision entirely to the staff
Listen to the reasons, explain the service must continue, and explore fair alternatives such as shift swaps
mcq.exp: 服务型领导要理解需要、找公平的替代方案，同时维持运营要求和问责；服务不等于批准每一项请求。

mcq.q: A manager humiliates an underperforming employee in front of colleagues, then says "I'm just being my authentic self." Which response best reflects the course's view of authentic leadership?
options: This is authentic leadership because the manager expressed real feelings
Authenticity is judged by sustained behaviour and requires respect and reflection; it does not justify humiliation
This shows relational transparency, which requires sharing all feelings
This is acceptable as long as the manager has an internalised moral perspective
mcq.exp: 真实性要看持续的行为，而且需要尊重和反思，不能拿来为羞辱开脱；关系透明也要判断什么适合说出来。

mcq.q: Which component of authentic leadership involves considering relevant evidence, including views that challenge one's own position, before deciding?
options: Balanced processing
Self-awareness
Relational transparency
Internalised moral perspective
mcq.exp: 平衡处理（balanced processing）就是决定前把相反的意见也当证据考虑进去，它不是简单折中。

mcq.q: A supervisor encourages staff to question assumptions behind the current workflow and to propose new methods. Which transformational component is this?
options: Idealised influence
Inspirational motivation
Individualised consideration
Intellectual stimulation
mcq.exp: 鼓励员工质疑假设、尝试新方法，这就是智力激发；个别化关怀是另一回事，它关注每个人各自的发展需要。

mcq.q: One supervisor checks report drafts during the process and corrects deviations early; another waits until a faulty report is submitted before acting. These illustrate, respectively:
options: Contingent reward and passive management by exception
Active and passive management by exception
Initiating structure and consideration
Transformational and transactional leadership
mcq.exp: 过程中检查并及早纠正是主动例外管理，等出错报告交上来才处理是被动例外管理；两者都是交易型领导的成分。

mcq.q: Which statement about transformational and transactional leadership is consistent with the lecture?
options: They are mutually exclusive types of people
Transactional leadership is a higher stage that replaces transformational leadership
They can complement each other in the same task, e.g. a shared vision plus agreed milestones and rewards
All successful leaders use a fixed mix of both
mcq.exp: 变革型和交易型可以在同一任务里互补，比如共同愿景加上约定的里程碑和奖励；它们不是互斥的两种人，也没有固定配方。

mcq.q: A new manager can approve budgets and assign projects, but staff take their difficult questions to a senior colleague whose knowledge and fairness they respect. The new manager has ___, while the senior colleague has ___.
options: status; power
power; status
both power and status; neither
leader emergence; leader effectiveness
mcq.exp: 新经理能批预算、派项目，这是权力，也就是控制别人在乎的资源；资深同事受大家尊重，这是地位。两者可以分开。

mcq.q: Galinsky et al. (2006), cited in the lecture, found that under experimental power conditions people:
options: Showed reduced perspective-taking, e.g. on the letter-E orientation task
Always ignored others' perspectives regardless of conditions
Became more accurate at understanding others' viewpoints
Gained higher social status automatically
mcq.exp: 研究发现，在特定实验条件下有权力的人换位思考变少了。这是一种倾向而非必然，所以领导要主动找反馈、检查假设。

match.title: Match each follower readiness level to the recommended Hersey–Blanchard style
Match each leadership concept to its key feature
pairs: Personal humility combined with professional will
Supporting followers' growth while keeping standards and accountability
Self-awareness, balanced processing, relational transparency, moral perspective
Idealised influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, individualised consideration
Contingent reward and management by exception
Rating of the least preferred coworker to identify task or relationship orientation

essay.q: Case: Mei is a senior analyst who has independently produced the company's monthly financial reports for three years. Her manager, Tom, is introducing a new data visualisation platform and plans to hand all reporting on the new platform to Mei with no guidance, saying "She's our best reporter, she'll be fine." Mei has never used the platform, but tells colleagues she is keen to learn it. Two weeks later her first dashboards are late and contain errors. Using the Hersey–Blanchard situational leadership model, diagnose the problem and recommend what Tom should do.
points: Readiness is task-specific: high readiness on routine reports (R4) does not transfer to the new platform
Diagnose ability (knowledge, skill) and willingness (motivation, confidence) separately: low ability but high willingness = R2
Tom used Delegating (S4) when Selling (S2) – high direction and high support – was needed
Recommend: demonstrate key steps, explain reasons, set practice and checkpoints, discuss drafts and recognise progress
Gradually reduce direction as evidence of competence grows; re-diagnose when the task changes
Note limits: Thompson & Vecchio (2009) gave limited support, so treat the prescription as a hypothesis and check other causes such as workload or resources
essay.model: Tom has made a readiness error. In the Hersey–Blanchard model, readiness combines ability (relevant knowledge and skill) and willingness (motivation and confidence) for a specific task. Mei is R4 for routine reporting, but the new platform is a different task: she lacks the relevant skill but is keen to learn, which places her at R2. Tom applied Delegating (S4) – low direction and low support – which suits only followers who are both able and willing. The late, error-filled dashboards are consistent with a mismatch rather than poor attitude. Tom should shift to Selling (S2): provide substantial task direction by demonstrating key steps, explaining why each part matters and setting clear quality standards and checkpoints, while also giving high relationship support by inviting questions, discussing drafts and recognising progress. As Mei's competence grows, Tom can reduce direction and move towards delegating, agreeing outcomes, deadlines and decision limits. However, Thompson and Vecchio (2009) found only limited support for the model, so Tom should treat R2 as a starting hypothesis: he should also check whether workload, inaccessible resources or unclear expectations contributed, try one form of support, and review the results before changing approach again.

essay.q: Case: Raj is a task-oriented manager (low LPC) who has been appointed to lead a cross-department IT project. The project goals are vague and acceptance criteria are undefined, team members distrust Raj because a previous manager broke promises, and Raj must seek approval from three department heads before he can allocate staff or budget. Senior management's plan is simply to tell Raj to "become more of a people person". Using Fiedler's contingency theory, analyse the situation and evaluate senior management's plan.
points: Explain LPC: low LPC = task-motivated, a relatively stable orientation
Diagnose the three favourability factors: poor leader–member relations, unstructured task, weak position power = situation VIII (very unfavourable)
Fiedler's pattern: task-oriented leaders tend to perform relatively better in very unfavourable situations; but the situation should still be improved where possible
Critique: Fiedler does not assume leaders can freely switch orientation, so asking Raj to change style is weak
Recommend changing the situation: clarify goals and acceptance criteria, clarify decision authority, rebuild trust by following through and involving members fairly
Note that authority does not automatically create trust, and the pattern is not a guarantee
essay.model: Fiedler's contingency theory argues that effectiveness depends on the fit between a leader's relatively stable motivational orientation, measured by the LPC scale, and situational favourability. Raj's low LPC indicates a task-motivated orientation. The three favourability factors are all unfavourable: leader–member relations are poor because of distrust, the task is unstructured because goals and acceptance criteria are vague, and position power is weak because Raj needs approval to allocate staff or budget. This corresponds to situation VIII, which the class diagram labels very unfavourable; in this zone the pattern shows task-oriented leaders performing relatively better, so Raj's orientation is not necessarily the problem. Senior management's plan is therefore poorly grounded: Fiedler treats LPC as relatively stable and does not assume leaders can switch orientation on demand. A better approach is to change the situation. Management can increase task structure by defining objectives and acceptance criteria, and strengthen position power by clarifying Raj's legitimate decision authority over resources. Separately, Raj should rebuild relations by following through on commitments and involving members fairly in decisions, because more authority will not automatically create trust. If fit still cannot be achieved, reassigning the leadership role could be considered. These interventions should be judged against evidence, since the eight-situation pattern is not a guarantee of performance.

essay.q: Case: Lena leads a customer service team that is rolling out a new booking system. She explains how the change will reduce customer waiting times, invites staff to challenge obstacles in the current process, and coaches newer staff individually. She also agrees clear milestones with each person and promises public recognition and a team bonus once targets are met. However, she rarely checks progress until a customer complaint arrives. Identify the leadership approaches evident in Lena's behaviour and evaluate their likely strengths and weaknesses.
points: Transformational: inspirational motivation (shared purpose), intellectual stimulation (challenging obstacles), individualised consideration (individual coaching)
Transactional – contingent reward: agreed milestones linked to recognition and bonus
Transactional – passive management by exception: intervening only after complaints
Transformational and transactional behaviours can complement each other; judge by observable behaviour
Weakness: passive monitoring lets problems grow; recommend active management by exception or regular checkpoints
Evaluate effectiveness with outcomes, member development, fairness and long-term consequences; note research links (Judge & Piccolo 2004) are correlational
essay.model: Lena's behaviour combines several leadership approaches. Explaining how the change benefits customers reflects inspirational motivation; inviting staff to challenge obstacles reflects intellectual stimulation; and coaching newer staff individually reflects individualised consideration – three of the four I's of transformational leadership. Her coaching and removal of barriers could also be read as servant-type behaviour. At the same time, agreeing milestones and linking them to recognition and a bonus is contingent reward, a transactional component that Judge and Piccolo (2004) found positively associated with satisfaction, motivation and performance, although these are correlations rather than proof of causation. These approaches complement each other: the vision supplies meaning while the milestones make delivery concrete. The weakness is in how Lena manages deviations. Waiting until a customer complaint arrives is passive management by exception, so errors may become serious before she acts. During a system rollout she should move to active management by exception, monitoring progress at agreed checkpoints and correcting problems early. Lena's effectiveness should then be judged not just by whether targets are met, but by member development, fair treatment of staff and longer-term outcomes such as trust and customer service quality.
